ECCF.Title: Encounter Crucible: Forge
ECCF.Subtitle: Generate a calculated encounter from an Actor folder.
ECCF.Settings.MenuHint: Configure an Actor folder and generate encounters through Encounter Crucible.
ECCF.Source.Title: Sources
ECCF.Source.Recursive: Include Actor folders below the selected folder
ECCF.Difficulty.Title: Target difficulty
ECCF.Strategy.Title: Composition strategy
ECCF.Strategy.QuantityHint: When selected alone, prefer reaching the target by using more individually weaker enemies. The maximum group size remains a hard cap.
ECCF.Strategy.StrengthHint: When selected alone, prefer fewer individually stronger enemies. Forge may still use more than one creature when a single Actor cannot reach the requested band.
ECCF.Strategy.FixedSizeHint: Require exactly the preferred/fixed group size. This overrides both scaling checkboxes; difficulty then changes through the available creature strength and composition.
ECCF.Strategy.Duplicates: Allow multiple copies of an Actor
ECCF.Strategy.DuplicatesHint: Enables groups of the same creature and repeated minions.
ECCF.Strategy.SameCrHint: Reduce large CR differences inside the encounter.
ECCF.Strategy.DiversityHint: Reward using several different Actors instead of only duplicates.
ECCF.Strategy.BossHint: Prefer a distinct primary creature. Difficulty is matched continuously; no Actor is globally excluded by an artificial XP ceiling.
ECCF.Strategy.MinionsHint: Prefer enough creatures to create meaningful group pressure.
ECCF.Errors.NoParty: The selected party source contains no characters.
ECCF.Errors.NoActors: The selected folder contains no usable NPC Actors with CR or XP data.
ECCF.Messages.Saved: Saved “{name}” as a {type} in Journal Directory → {folder}.
ECCF.Strategy.BossEncounterHint: Strongly require a distinctly stronger primary creature. When the filtered pool cannot satisfy this shape, Forge returns the closest roster with a warning instead of failing.
ECCF.Preferences.Title: Creature preferences
ECCF.Preferences.MultiSelectHint: Select one or more ancestries. No selection means any ancestry. Without strict mode, Forge prefers plain matches but may use a minority of other creatures.
ECCF.Preferences.StrictRacesHint: Only plain Actors matching at least one selected ancestry may be used. Transformative variants such as Human Shapechangers require their qualifier to be selected under archetypes.
ECCF.Preferences.Archetypes: Preferred classes, types, archetypes, or themes
ECCF.Preferences.ArchetypeHint: No selection means any class/type. Values come from D&D5e creature type, qualifiers, class, subclass, features, and useful Actor-name terms. “Any Race” and “Any Class” metadata are ignored as wildcards.
ECCF.Preferences.StrictArchetypesHint: Only Actors matching at least one selected class, type, archetype, or theme may be used.
ECCF.Actions.AddToCombatHint: Use the active combat for this scene, or create one when necessary.
ECCF.Storage.Explanation: Save creates a readable Journal Entry below Journal Directory → Encounter Crucible. Forge can sort it into a theme subfolder and names it with absolute party context using the configured format string.
ECCF.Messages.MissingActors: {count} Actors could no longer be resolved and were not placed.
ECCF.Storage.CustomNameHint: This value fills {name}. The configured format adds party context, difficulty, or any other selected placeholders. Duplicate final names receive (2), (3), and so on.
ECCF.Settings.OrganizeThemeHint: Create and use theme subfolders below the Encounter Crucible Journal folder.
ECCF.Settings.ThemeModeHint: Choose how Forge derives the Journal subfolder for a saved encounter.
ECCF.Settings.ThemeArchetype: Dominant class, type, archetype, or theme
ECCF.Settings.FallbackThemeHint: Used when Forge cannot infer a useful race, type, class, archetype, or theme.
ECCF.Settings.NameFormatHint: Format string for the final Journal name. Available placeholders: {name}, {difficulty}, {theme}, {partySize}, {averageLevel}, {minimumLevel}, {maximumLevel}, {totalPartyLevels}, {partyLevels}, {enemyCount}, {averageCr}, {minimumCr}, {maximumCr}, {date}. Default: [P{partySize}-L{averageLevel}-{difficulty}] {name}.
ECCF.Preferences.GlobalFilterHint: Compound values and the visible race/archetype vocabulary are controlled globally under Configure Settings → Module Settings → Encounter Crucible: Forge.
ECCF.Settings.SplitCompoundTraits: Split compound race and archetype values
ECCF.Settings.SplitCompoundTraitsHint: Recommended. Turns values such as “Human, Shapechanger” or “Humanoid (Shapechanger)” into separate selectable entries. This also improves strict matching and automatic theme names.
ECCF.Settings.RaceWhitelistHint: Optional comma-, semicolon-, or newline-separated values or wildcard patterns. When set, only matching race and creature-kind tags appear in Forge. Example: Human, Goblin, Elf*. Actors themselves are not removed.
ECCF.Settings.RaceBlacklistHint: Optional values or wildcard patterns removed from Forge after the whitelist is applied. Example: Shapechanger or Shape* hides those tags while retaining the Actor and its other tags.
ECCF.Settings.ArchetypeWhitelistHint: Optional comma-, semicolon-, or newline-separated values or wildcard patterns. When set, only matching class, type, archetype, and theme tags appear in Forge.
ECCF.Settings.ArchetypeBlacklistHint: Optional values or wildcard patterns removed after the archetype whitelist. Useful for generic or noisy tags such as Humanoid, Commoner, or words derived from Actor names.
ECCF.WindowGeometry.MenuHint: Clear this client’s saved Forge window position and dimensions and return the window to its default centred layout.
ECCF.WindowGeometry.ResetExplanation: Reset the saved position and size of the Encounter Crucible: Forge window for this browser client?
ECCF.WindowGeometry.ResetHint: This does not change world settings or another GM’s layout. An open Forge window is immediately resized and centred.
ECCF.WindowGeometry.ResetComplete: The Forge window position and size were reset.
ECCF.Saved.Title: Saved encounters
ECCF.Saved.UseCurrentPartyHint: Replace the party stored in the Journal with the currently selected party source. Disable this to restore the encounter exactly as it was saved.
ECCF.Saved.Empty: No Encounter Crucible Journals have been saved yet.
ECCF.Errors.SavedEncounterMissing: The selected saved encounter no longer exists or no longer contains Encounter Crucible data.
ECCF.Messages.Loaded: Loaded “{name}” into Forge and recalculated it.
ECCF.Strategy.BossSafetyHint: Boss-like means compositionally distinct, not automatically safe. Lower slider positions strongly penalize excessive overmatch; Extreme deliberately permits deadly and overwhelming candidates.
ECCF.Result.UnsafeExcludedHint: One or more Actors were excluded because their individual XP exceeded the safety limit for this party and target difficulty.
ECCF.Result.OvermatchedWarning: This encounter is an overwhelming mismatch for the current party. It is rated Extreme regardless of model averaging and should not be treated as an ordinary boss encounter.
ECCF.Result.NoHardLimitHint: Forge first satisfies strict filters, then the requested difficulty band, selected ancestry/archetype preferences, and the chosen composition mode. Quantity and strength are real search targets rather than minor tie-breakers. Extreme remains uncapped.
ECCF.Result.QualifiedRaceExcluded: Transformative matches excluded by strict mode
ECCF.Strategy.ModeHint.neutral: Neither scaling checkbox is selected. Forge chooses the closest difficulty without preferring enemy count or individual creature strength.
ECCF.Strategy.ModeHint.quantity: Only Additional Enemies is selected. Moving right primarily increases enemy count and prefers lower XP per creature.
ECCF.Strategy.ModeHint.strength: Only Stronger Enemies is selected. Moving right primarily increases XP/CR per creature and keeps the roster comparatively small.
ECCF.Strategy.ModeHint.balanced: Both are selected. Forge uses a hybrid target between quantity-only and strength-only: difficulty may rise through both more enemies and stronger enemies.
ECCF.Strategy.ModeHint.fixed: Fixed group size takes precedence over both scaling checkboxes. Forge always generates exactly the configured count and adjusts the available creature strength within it.

ECCF.Errors.CompatibilityReason.api-vers: Encounter Crucible exposes an invalid Helper API version
ECCF.Errors.CompatibilityReason.api-majo: The Encounter Crucible Helper API major version is incompatible
ECCF.Errors.CompatibilityReason.api-vers: The Encounter Crucible Helper API is older than the required version
ECCF.Errors.CompatibilityReason.capabili: The Encounter Crucible API lacks a required capability
ECCF.Source.ClearFolderHint: Clear the selected enemy Actor folder.
ECCF.Source.ToggleFolder: Expand or collapse this folder branch
ECCF.Source.ActorCountsHint: Direct Actors / Actors including all descendant folders
ECCF.Source.FolderPickerHint: {count} Actor folders available. Search matches folder names and full paths; parent folders remain visible so hierarchy is preserved.
ECCF.Source.NoActorFolders: No world Actor folders were found. Create an Actor folder in the Actors sidebar, then reopen or rerender Forge.
